content.text: Xingwan, as the end of the semester approaches, I’ve just finished organizing the GitHub contribution chart for this academic year and wanted to share it with you. There are two noticeable coding peaks in March and October—the one in March corresponds exactly to when we started the health dashboard project. Remember how I stayed up all night writing scripts to monitor Git commit times? The peak in October was likely during the development phase of the public opinion analysis heatmap and the information aggregator demo. It feels like such a fulfilling year!

Wow, Chenguang, your submission records are so dense, truly a tech maniac! It reminds me of when we collaborated on the health dashboard project—you were just as dedicated back then. The screenshot of the health data dashboard you shared had a sleep curve like a rollercoaster, and the sedentary warnings lit up a whole row of red lights. I’ve just organized the annual data for the public account too—take a look when you have a moment.

This is the list of the top ten most-read articles on my public account this year, ranging from coverage of the welcome party to planning for the cultural festival. It feels like I've been dealing with words and events all year long. Look, the review article on the digital art exhibition also made the list—that was from the time we went to the '纹以载道' exhibition, and you were explaining particle systems and sensor latency to me back then.

That's amazing! Your reading data is really impressive, especially that article about stray animals on campus. Is it related to the cat guide project we discussed earlier? I remember you also joined the animal protection club and sent me that rough Excel list and animal photos, asking if we could create a mini-program.

Exactly! That article was inspired by our collaboration. Later, I also used the animal adoption mini-program prototype you developed for promotion, and the number of stars grew quite quickly! Your technical expertise was a huge help. Just as we discussed earlier, you bring the technology, and I provide the content and promotion to help "cat seniors" and "dog juniors" find homes. This collaborative model is incredibly effective.

Haha, you're too kind! Actually, I really admire your planning skills. From health management to game collaborations, and then to digital art exhibitions, you always find interesting angles. I remember during that game collaboration, your proposal outline mentioned exploring the formation of默契 in non-verbal cooperation, and we actually observed it when we played *It Takes Two*. Oh, and I also shared a comparison chart summarizing our respective achievements.

Look, on the left are my GitHub codes and project achievements, ranging from health dashboards and campus cat guides to information aggregators and public opinion heat maps. On the right are your public accounts and campus activities, from social supervision of health projects and gaming field research to retrospectives of digital art exhibitions and animal protection advocacy. It feels like we’ve been sprinting on different tracks this year, yet there are so many intersections, just like the overlapping lines in this diagram.

This comparison is so interesting! Chen Guang, your execution ability is truly impressive. The health dashboard, the information aggregation script, and the hotspot map concept for public opinion analysis—all of these were implemented quickly. On my side, it’s more about communication and experience. For example, the 'real-time commentary' analysis during the game collaboration—do you remember the physics simulation you analyzed when my character fell? And during the digital art exhibition, the dual-perspective observation report we created on 'technology-experience.'

Yes, every collaboration teaches me something new. For instance, the health dashboard project—your suggestions for the social accountability module and the points-based incentive system made me realize the importance of human-centered design beyond just technology. This will likely be helpful for my future job applications at major tech companies, especially since user experience is so emphasized nowadays. Just like you said back then, reframing health issues as engaging projects that require technological solutions.

I think so too! From you, I've learned how to use technology to solve practical problems. For instance, the idea of a cyber campus tool to address information anxiety—your Python script approach gave me more confidence during my media operations internship. I'm actually looking for an internship in internet operations right now. Remember when I complained about missing lecture registrations and being overwhelmed by all the @everyone notifications in various group chats on my phone? Your concept for an information aggregator demo perfectly addressed that pain point.

Then we complement each other! Technology changes the world, but communication makes the change visible. Just like the campus cat guide, without your promotion, it might have remained just a cold little app. By the way, do you remember the discussion about emotional reactions to failure during our game collaboration? You took a screenshot of the character's comical death moment and said that sharing such humorous failures helps relieve real-life stress.

Of course I remember! That 'field research' was super interesting. Your technical review combined with my experience notes came in handy later during the digital art exhibition recap—we analyzed audience interaction methods, you from a technical perspective and me from an experiential one. This kind of cross-disciplinary exchange is truly a valuable asset, far more meaningful than just grinding away at technology or organizing events. Just like we said after the exhibition, we went from ordinary interactions to project partners and then to research collaborators.

Completely agree! Open-source sharing and diverse experiences—our core values actually align quite well. Looking back on the academic year, I feel like I’ve not only written more code but also learned how to collaborate better with others. I have to thank you for stepping in during my health crisis, haha—remember when my terminal was flashing red alerts and my caffeine intake was 200% over the limit? You said, "You’re trading your health for code," and then proposed a "geek-friendly" health intervention plan.

Oh, don't mention it! Back then, when I saw the red alert on your terminal, I thought, "This needs to be tackled as a technical project." Looking back now, from health management to public welfare initiatives, we've collaborated all the way, and our relationship has evolved from ordinary interactions to research partners. Every session feels like unlocking a new level—from health crises to gaming collaborations, pet encyclopedias, information aggregation, public opinion analysis, and even digital art exhibitions. Our collaborative chain keeps growing richer and richer.

Exactly, each session feels like unlocking a new level. As the academic year ends, even though we may go our separate ways in the future, I will always remember this collaborative model. Your achievements have shown me the power of communication, and I wish you great success in the media field! Just as you said during the digital art exhibition, freedom of expression and diverse experiences are important, and you have truly embodied that.

Thank you, Chenguang! Keep up the great work too. The aesthetic sense of tech enthusiasts is quite impressive these days, as evidenced by digital art exhibitions—the angles you chose when taking photos for me back then were spot on, proving that tech enthusiasts have a keen eye for aesthetics! I hope we can continue collaborating in the future, whether on technical projects or leisure activities. Having completed the academic year review, I feel a clearer sense of my own growth, much like tracking progress with data in our health dashboard project.

Well, confirming each other's value is the best way to wrap things up. Let's stay in touch and collaborate again on future projects or exhibitions! Just like we said during our game collaboration, lifelong learning knows no bounds, and changing the world through technology starts with small steps.

Deal! I'll focus on finals first, and we'll catch up later. Remember, the health board's point incentives are still active—don't pull another all-nighter programming. I don't want to see a row of red lights for prolonged sitting.
